title: Halfords says a third-party digital service was hit after extortion group n0n listed it; Halfords found no evidence customer information was involved
date_note: road.cc (25 Nov) says Halfords puts the attack in the previous week; the page gives no earlier exact day, so the publication day is used.
geo_basis: country as stated by the source (UK retailer); no city given
summary: road.cc reports that the extortion group n0n listed Halfords on its dark web site among companies it says it obtained data from. Halfords describes a "security issue involving a third-party digital service" affecting "limited product information and some employee usernames". Halfords says it found no evidence that passwords, payment details or customer information were involved, and that its own systems were not accessed.
plain: The n0n extortion group listed Halfords on its site. Halfords says a third-party service was affected, with limited product information and some employee usernames, and that it found no evidence customer information was involved.
exec: Halfords says a third-party service incident touched limited product information and some employee usernames; it found no evidence customer information was involved.
action: Halfords says no action is required from customers.

sources.name: road.cc: Halfords data hacked by international extortion gang
The Journal: Bicycle retailer Halfords hit by cyberattack, but states no customer data accessed

validation.note: road.cc and thejournal.ie (The Journal), independent publishers, each relay Halfords statement on a third-party digital service issue, limited product information and some employee usernames.

review.note: Compared title, date, Halfords statement quotes and no-action line against road.cc and The Journal
